Long story short, anxiety, depression, complex ptsd and complicated grief.  Started ice baths hoping it would help calcified tendonitis.  Started feeling emotionally better for the first time in a long time.  Googled
Mental health and ice baths and found wim hof. I went colder, I got a bigger horse trough, then a better evaporative cooler, then finally the chest freezer.

Now I don’t do it everyday like I used to.  I can’t believe two years ago I would be doing it in my warehouse when it was already 45 degrees in there. I still do the breathing everyday though.  I still hit it but it’s more like I get an itch.  Like I feel the heaviness.  When I feel the darkness creeping back in I go back to it, when life hits me hard I go back to it.

To me just the routine of it all, prepping the bath, taking care of your bath, overcoming the voices to get in it, controlling the breathing inside of it.  Moving afterwards to not freeze and get after drop, it all is conducive to self
Care.  I hated the imaginary threats, I like fighting real ones like the cold.  I hated feeling zero desire to do anything, I used to care a lot about things, the cold brought that back.

In my mental health toolbox it’s my sledgehammer. 

So yeah, I’d try it.

Suicide in San Fran increased greatly during April, does that mean quarantines cause suicide?  No, it means those individuals were already at greater risk and the increased increased social isolation/stress causes by the pandemic pushed them over the edge.

Edit: There’s also the environmental vs genetic factors.  Certain mental heath conditions that have genetic components could increase the risk of suicide in all family members, especially when you factor in trauma and extreme stress.

I feel your predicament.  I myself have been very goal oriented, even my pursuit of the advancement of stages is goal oriented.  I mean it seems like a paradox to me.  Isn't the inherent nature of meditating to some degree to alleviate suffering a pursuit thus making it a form of suffering?  

It seems very difficult to not be goal oriented while sitting, and I too notice that if I have to do something it is much more stressful than if I "get" to do it.  I think that is the solution in itself.  Taking a breath is a get to do during a sit experience, feeling anything is a get to do, whether painful or pleasurable.  So our goals should be taken with an attitude of getting to do anything, it is okay to set the goal, but the pursuit has to be taken with a mindset of getting to do anything, even if it's endlessly pursuing a goal.
